chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdallah ibn Sinan, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Nothing becomes apparent to Allah concerning something except that it was in His knowledge before it appears to Him.

key_terms.بَدَا: Bada' (manifestation or apparent change of divine decree)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between Allah's eternal knowledge and the concept of Bada'?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith clarifies that 'Bada'' is not a change in Allah's essential knowledge (Ilm al-Dhati) but rather the manifestation of a specific decree within His eternal knowledge, often linked to the concept of 'Ilm al-Irtibati' (sequential knowledge). This distinction preserves divine omniscience while allowing for dynamic events in creation, such as the alteration of destiny through supplication or good deeds, as elaborated by scholars like Al-Sharif al-Murtada and Al-Tusi.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/364] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Husayn b. Sa’id from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abdallah b. Sinan from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
Nothing becomes apparent to Allah concerning something (to make Him change His decree) except that it was in His knowledge before it appears to Him (to change it).
